bottleneck: Schizophrenia involves 100+ risk variants, disrupted dopamine and glutamate signaling, and developmental circuit miswiring — yet no model connects genes to symptoms. Antipsychotics block dopamine and blunt psychosis while leaving cognitive and negative symptoms untouched, suggesting the treated pathway is downstream of the real pathology. The core circuit defect remains unidentified after a century of study, and without it, drug discovery is limited to refining a 1950s mechanism.
current_state: All approved drugs share the dopamine-blocking mechanism discovered in the 1950s. Glutamate and circuit-based approaches are in trials but unproven, and no novel mechanism has reached approval.

title: Schizophrenia's core circuit defect unidentified
why_it_blocks: Seventy years of dopamine blockade manages psychosis without touching cognition or motivation — the symptoms that actually disable. Finding the real circuit defect would open the first new mechanism in generations.
